proof_summary: For \(1\le n<10\), the partner \(k=10n\) works. For \(n\ge10\), writing \(d=D(n)\), \(A=D(d-1)\), \(B=D(2d-1)\), digit-sum congruences modulo \(9\) and elementary bounds produce \(L=(n+A-B)/9\) with \(d\le10^L\); a decimal-complement calculation then gives \(D(d(2\cdot10^L-1))=9L+B-A=n\), so this positive, distinct number is divisible by \(D(n)\) and its digit sum divides \(n\).
